recap.workouts:
Class at 06:06 — Chrissy. The morning is on file as a single Workout of 119:52, which is the class and the twenty gym sets logged together rather than a two-hour metcon: 3,157 m accumulated across the bike and the runs, average heart rate 120, peak 171, load 52, your RPE 8. Your note: pushed harder than prescribed. The call was FITNESS, the 200 m option on both runs and a steady echo bike, and you took more than that. Peak 171 sits above your run threshold heart rate of 167. Recorded, not scolded — and the only reason it matters is that it is the one thing in today's file that explains how the run felt four hours later.

Gym, upper pull plus triceps, twenty of twenty sets:

Lat pulldown 210 — 12/12/12/12. TRIGGER FIRED. Against 12/12/9/8 at the same load on 2 Sep that is not a marginal step; it is four clean sets where you had two. 220 lb on the next pull day.

Barbell row 85 — 11/12/12/12, against 8/9/10 on 2 Sep. One rep off a sweep on the opening set, so 85 holds and 90 stays unearned. Second session running where the reps climbed inside the set rather than fading — that is not what an unmanageable load looks like.

Face pull 95 — 20/20/18/17. The trigger reads across all eight of the week's sets and wants 20 on every one, so 95 holds and 100 is out of reach this week. The first two sets were at the ceiling; the last two were twenty sets of pulling talking.

Barbell curl — you ran 65, not the 60 on the sheet, and returned 9/9/9/9. Straight about both halves of that: the written condition for 65 was twelve reps on all eight of the week's sets and it had not fired, so the load was taken early. The reps then defended it — 9 is inside the 8-12 range on every single set, which is what a working load looks like rather than one that beat you. I am not going to pretend the trigger fired, and I am not going to ask you to walk it back tomorrow.

Overhead triceps extension 150 — 12/12/12/12. TRIGGER FIRED, against 12/12/11/10 on 2 Sep. 160 lb earned. Triceps is the priority muscle and that is a clean sweep on the long-head movement.

Your note on the visit: it felt hard because it took so long. Twenty sets is the biggest single visit of the week and an RPE 7 on that is duration, not load.

RF6 — 45:02 against 45 prescribed, 8.01 km, average pace 5:37/km, load 45, average heart rate 139, peak 160, your RPE 7. And it paired: a planned event for today did appear on the calendar after all, so it scored 97.8 percent compliance where this morning's card said it would score nothing at all.

Read off the per-second trace against your own zone file rather than any interval table. RF6 prescribes no Zone 3 work rep, so there are no reps to segment and the whole 45 minutes is the read — that is the module saying so, not a gap in it.

Time in zone, computed from the stream against your bands: 11:01 Zone 1, 32:14 Zone 2, 1:50 Zone X, nothing above. Prescribed was 10 minutes Zone 1 and 35 Zone 2. Forty-three of the forty-five minutes were easy. You had exactly one job on this run — hold the ceiling down — and 1:50 of Zone X across three quarters of an hour is about as close to perfect as that job gets. Your average pace landed at 5:37 in the slow half of a band whose fast end is 5:01, on an afternoon when drifting up would have been the easiest thing in the world.

The heart rate story is the honest complication. Average 139 sits square inside your run Zone 2 band of 135 to 150 and the peak of 160 never came near threshold, so nothing here is alarming. But heart rate climbed about a beat a minute across the session, and the second half ran roughly 12 percent more expensive than the first at the same pace. Part of that is mechanical — the warm-up sits inside the first half, and heart rate starting from cold always flatters it — but not all of it, and it lines up precisely with what you wrote: felt harder than it should have. Your own 7 against the watch's automatic 5 says the same thing twice.

What it indicates, confidence stated. The execution was excellent and the aerobic cost of that pace was higher than this pace normally costs you. The likeliest reading is the morning: a metcon ridden past its scaling cue plus twenty gym sets, four hours earlier. That is a same-day explanation and I am treating it as one — it buys nothing beyond today. Consequence: proceed.
recap.takeaways:
1) THE RUN VERDICT — EXECUTED, AND THESE WERE THE RIGHT 45 MINUTES. Structure held, 97.8 percent compliance, 43 of 45 minutes genuinely easy and Zone X kept to under two. This was the most load-bearing easy session left in the week: Monday's hour never happened and Tuesday's ride stopped after one rep, so the week had been running under its 80 percent easy floor and there was no spare easy volume anywhere to replace these minutes with. You banked every one of them, and you banked them by running slower than you had to rather than faster. Confidence high — this is the per-second trace, not an interval table.

2) THE MORNING IS THE ONE CAVEAT, AND IT IS A CAVEAT ABOUT TIMING RATHER THAN ABOUT EFFORT. Chrissy was the biggest metcon of the week, the call was the FITNESS column with short runs and a steady bike, and you pushed past it four hours before a session the week could not afford to lose. It cost you nothing today — the run still landed. But the run cost more than it should have, and that is the bill. On a day carrying a protected easy session, the class is the lever and it is the only one.

3) ADAPT: NO-OP, AND TWO TRIGGERS PAID OUT. Class MODIFIED upward rather than failed, gym EXECUTED at twenty of twenty, RF6 EXECUTED at full structure. Nothing in the remaining week moves and nothing needed to — the protection a hard session would normally ask for is already built in, because Friday carries no endurance and no leg-heavy class work, so Saturday's RCI3 still starts off the freshest legs in the block. Lat pulldown earns 220 and overhead triceps extension earns 160.

4) TOMORROW IS THE SESSION MOST AT RISK IN THE WEEK, AND IT IS FLAGGED RATHER THAN PRE-CUT. Four muscles close on Friday — side delts, rear delts, biceps and triceps — so if the gym visit goes, the week lands at 36 of 51 sets and the engine ramps from the actual next week. That is what the brake is for and it is not a disaster. The class is at 05:00, well clear of an afternoon departure, and there is no endurance session to fit around it.

Three pieces today, and the one that mattered was executed properly.

06:00 Cutthroat — 56' gym block, avg HR 112, max 151, load 20, RPE 5. You took 135 lb on the clean and jerks and normal wall walks rather than the light-bar [FITNESS] version I called for, plus the 60 single unders per round. Honest flag: on the lowest readiness morning of the block, that was the version with the most room to go wrong. It didn't — avg HR 112 and max 151 say you genuinely cruised it, and 21 total C&J reps at 135 sits well inside your strength. Noted, not scolded.

Arms and delts, the full Friday dose at exactly the deload loads: triceps pushdown 135 × 13, barbell curl 40 × 12, lateral raise 20 × 20. You were right about the Sorinex station — those are hamstring curls, so substituting your own barbell curls was the correct read, and the class banded face pulls covered the rear delts.

RAn4 — 45:03, 7.27 km, load 37 against a planned 45, RPE 5, paired cleanly to the planned session. The file splits exactly to the prescription: 15:01 warm-up, then 4 × (2:30 hard / 5:00 jog). Nothing missing, nothing added. The 82% compliance figure is intervals.icu scoring against its own preset zones, not a shortfall — every step is there at full length.

Warm-up: 5:56/km, HR 119 avg, max 132. Honest Z1.

The four reps, target band 3:48–4:17/km:
rep 1 — 4:08/km, HR 131 at the gun to 158 by the end
rep 2 — 4:03/km, 120 to 161
rep 3 — 4:08/km, 126 to 162
rep 4 — 4:03/km, 130 to 176

All four inside the band, total spread across the set five seconds per kilometre, and the last rep tied the fastest. That is exactly the shape this session wants: crisp, repeatable, no decay.

The HR story — and this is precisely why interval averages are useless here: rep 2 carries a LOWER average than rep 1 despite being five seconds per km quicker, purely because you started it from 120 instead of 131. Read the peaks instead: 158 · 161 · 162 · 176. The first three climb four beats in total across the set, which is a tightly controlled ladder. Rep 4 jumps 14 beats at exactly rep 2's pace — a slice of that is the 5 m of climbing inside that rep, the rest is you closing the session hard. 176 is the highest heart rate in your file this block, above Thursday's 173, and it sits at the top of the new Z4 band (167–175), so rep 4 is the only rep that reached Zone 4 by heart rate. Reps 1–3 peaked 158–162, i.e. high Z3. On 2.5-minute reps starting from a fully recovered HR that is normal lag, not a soft effort — pace is the sharp target here, and pace was hit every time.

Recoveries: 8:12 · 9:07 · 8:58 · 8:39 per km, HR dropping to 108 · 101 · 113 · 114. You shed 50-plus beats between every rep. On the day the panel called your worst of the block, that is a body still recovering fast.

Method note: analysed off the workout-matched interval table, which maps 1:1 to the prescribed steps (901 s warm-up, then 150 s / 300 s four times). The per-second stream pass wasn't available this evening — the Drive folder didn't mount into the compute sandbox — so pace is per-rep rather than per-second. Nothing above is estimated.
recapPrev.takeaways:
1) The run verdict: clean. Four reps inside the pace band, five seconds per km of spread across the whole set, the last one tied fastest, HR shedding 50+ beats in every recovery, and no fatigue signal anywhere. Load 37 — a fraction of Thursday. As stimulus maintenance it did exactly its job.

2) The call, straight. I recommended cutting RAn4 this morning at readiness 27 and you ran it — second day running that you overrode me and the file came back clean. What I actually think, rather than just conceding: the execution was good, and a load of 37 is not what turns a deload into Week 4 again. But two overrides in two days is a pattern worth naming, and the readiness signal — sleeping HR elevated a fifth straight morning, breathing now flagged too, Form −25.8 — still hasn't been paid for. One well-run session doesn't settle it. Tomorrow is where it gets settled.

3) ADAPT: no-op. RAn4 EXECUTED at full structure, Cutthroat done heavier than called but genuinely easy by HR, hypertrophy exact at the deload dose. Nothing in the remaining week moves — and on a deload nothing gets added, ever.

4) Lateral raise 20 lb × 20 tops the range: banked, not applied, per the deload rule. Week 9 now opens with lat pulldown to 190, face pull to 85, leg curl to 50, overhead triceps ext up one step, and lateral raise up one step. Five bumps waiting, all earned this week without spending them.

2026-09-12.mind: Four by eight minutes at 4:22 to 4:42 per kilometre, in a place I do not know, off a full day with nothing in it — pacing that so rep four still exists is a skill, and getting deliberately better at a hard thing is the point.

end.name: RCI3 — 64′ (4 × 8′ Z3)
end.detail: This gets the freshest legs of the week and that is not an accident: Friday carries no endurance and no leg-heavy class work, so this is the only hard session in the block that starts from a genuine rest day. It is the one good thing the travel constraint bought.
end.desc:
5′ Z1 @ 5:45–7:17/km, 5′ Z2 @ 5:01–5:45/km, 4 × (8′ Z3 @ 4:22–4:42/km / 3′ Z1), 5′ Z2, 5′ Z1. (Verified 2026-08-30.)
Thirty-two minutes of threshold running — the largest block of hard time in the week. Eight minutes is long enough that pacing decides everything: go out at 4:22 and rep four will not exist. Open rep 1 at the slow end of the band and let it come to you.
If the route is unfamiliar or hilly, run the reps on heart rate (Z3 = 161–167) rather than fighting the pace band on terrain. Rolling-terrain scatter is the ground, not an execution fault.
It travels — shoes and a road.

mob.when: right after the run, while you are still warm
mob.desc: 2 × 45–60 s per side each. Squeeze the down-side glute FIRST, then lean — the tuck is the exercise, not the lean. No class tomorrow morning, so nothing is compromised by it.

mob.name: 90/90 hip lift with full exhale
mob.desc: 5 breaths × 2–3 sets. Full exhale is the whole exercise. Not within ~90 minutes of a large meal.

2026-09-13.mind: Three ten-minute blocks at 5:01 to 5:45 with the rest genuinely slow, which is a harder discipline than running fast — hours like this are what make me the one who still says yes to the long day out with Fleur in twenty years.

end.name: RAe1 — 60′ aerobic-interval run
end.detail: READ THE STRUCTURE BEFORE YOU RUN IT. RAe1 is the SMALLEST workout in the RAe family — nothing like week 13's RAe10. Only 30 of the 60 minutes are Zone 2. Closing the week on the smaller of the two runs is deliberate: it leaves week 15 opening on a clean Monday.
end.desc:
10′ Z1 @ 5:45–7:17/km, 3 × (10′ Z2 @ 5:01–5:45/km / 3′ Z1), 10′ Z1. (Pulled live 2026-09-07.)
This is not an hour of Zone 2 — it is three ten-minute Z2 blocks inside twenty-nine minutes of Zone 1.
Finishing the last Z2 block and never coming back down turns the tail into Zone X, which is the classic way this session type goes wrong and the exact error RAe10 was flagged for.
The three-minute floats are short and that is the point. They are floats, not recoveries — so the Z2 blocks have to be genuinely Z2 rather than an assault.
(Segments sum to 59′ against the library's stated 60 — their rounding, not a missing segment.)
